attempted_contrary_interfaces: Identical test behavior treated as unique artifact identity.
A green pipeline treated as exposure authority.
An approved model treated as actual deployed state.
The same test counted as independent evidence twice.
All evidence discarded after harmless change.
All evidence carried after a changed critical premise.
A trace link treated as proof of the linked claim.

positive_controls.argument: Current operating rationale and known limitations give incident observations context and preserve why a corrective action was chosen.
Recoverable event-time versions and baseline status make the observed outcome attributable to the correct product and relevant change.
Reconciled operating configuration and explicit unknowns delimit what the incident evidence actually describes.
Delegated emergency authority, impact analysis and post-change obligations define the admissible corrective action and its receiving evidence.
Versioned semantics and two-sided ownership guide the interpretation of the incident and the appropriate corrective responsibility.
A discriminating evidence method and acceptance condition define how the proposed corrective action will be checked.
Failure-level analysis guides which additional observation or controlled interaction check is needed to interpret the incident and verify correction.
Accurate configuration and claim links identify affected obligations and let later investigators recover the correction rationale.
Explicit assumptions and defeaters identify which operational signals matter to the assurance conclusion and require action.
Persistent problem identity, affected states and authorized residuals prevent incident learning from dissolving into a backlog or false closure.
Model semantics, provenance and version relationships identify how an observation should update or challenge the model.
Traceable evidence generation and promotion decisions connect operational findings to the candidate state and authorized response.
